the decoherence of a quantum particle due to a weak linearly perturbed spacetime is a consequence of the quantum nature of spacetime and the matter–gravity coupling; and that the decoherence is in the energy basis of the quantum particle, and depends on the spacetime texture.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we derive a master equation for a matter field in a perturbed spacetime based on quantum field theory in curved spacetime and the equivalence principle, and that the decoherence rates depend on extra parameters other then the Planck scale.

the master equation for gravitational decoherence we derived from first principles has a form similar to that in quantum Brownian motion, but with a different decoherence rate, and that the decoherence is in the energy basis rather than in the position basis.

we have derived a general quantum field theory master equation for the dynamics of a quantum matter system in the presence of a weak gravitational perturbation, and that this master equation predicts gravitational decoherence, in contrast to the usual expectation that the gravitational field is not a decohering environment.

gravitational decoherence is a robust phenomenon, and it can be studied without invoking extra ingredients.
the quantum nature of gravity is not only an open problem in physics, but it is also a problem of physics.
